title: libvirt virtual machine disks
whyItMatters: Virtual machines run by libvirt keep their disk images here, each a complete guest system with its own files. They are large and are not removed when the machine definition is deleted.
source: libvirt storage documentation: the default directory storage pool for qemu:///system is /var/lib/libvirt/images: https://libvirt.org/storage.html
notes: Normally root-only, hence requiresElevation. Session VMs (qemu:///session) keep their disks in ~/.local/share/libvirt/images, and custom pools can point anywhere, so this rule does not see every VM.

cleanup.exportFirst: Copy any needed virtual machine disk images or exported guest files to an external drive before deleting them.
steps: Open your virtual machine app (Virtual Machine Manager or GNOME Boxes) and shut down the guests.
Delete each unwanted guest and its storage in the app; an administrator password may be required.
The root-owned images folder named in the plan is left to the full reset.
cleanup.risk: Permanently deletes all selected virtual machine disk images and guest operating system contents.
